_comment: Starting points for the console task editor (Tasks tab, Template). text is the script, one line per entry. Entries with verify=true: test them on a VM before deploying.

templates.name: Sync-Clock
templates.description: Sync the clock with the domain (or time.windows.com) right after setup
templates.notes: Domain PCs sync with a domain controller, others with time.windows.com.
text: rem A PC captured before a daylight saving change can start an hour off; Kerberos and the domain join need the right time.

templates.name: Enable-RemoteDesktop
templates.description: Turn on Remote Desktop with Network Level Authentication and open the firewall for it
templates.notes: Who may connect is still set by the Remote Desktop Users group or a GPO.
text: # The group's resource id works in every Windows language, unlike its display name.

templates.name: Power-NoSleepOnAC
templates.description: Never sleep on mains power; screen off after 30 minutes
templates.notes: Handy for lab and classroom PCs that get updates and remote reimaging at night.

templates.name: Remove-ConsumerApps
templates.description: Remove Xbox, Solitaire and other consumer Store apps for new users
templates.notes: Test on a VM first; better still, remove them from the reference PC before capture.
text: # Removes the provisioned copies, so the apps aren't installed for users who log on later.
# Edit the list to suit; names are wildcards matched against DisplayName.

templates.name: Copy-DeployLogs
templates.description: Copy the deployment logs to a share, in a folder named after the PC
templates.notes: Put it last in the answer file so the other tasks are in the logs. Replace REPLACE_SHARE in the arguments.
text: # Runs as SYSTEM, so the share sees the computer account: give Domain Computers write access to it.
if ($Share -like 'REPLACE*') { Write-Output 'Set the share in the task arguments: -Share \\server\Logs'; exit 1 }

templates.name: Set-DesktopWallpaper
templates.description: Set the desktop and lock screen picture for every user (Enterprise and Education)
templates.notes: Import a folder holding this script and wallpaper.jpg, or add the picture to the task folder afterwards.
text: # Put the picture in this task's folder (Import from: Folder...). Uses the PersonalizationCSP keys,
# which Windows only honours on Enterprise and Education editions.
if (-not (Test-Path $src)) { Write-Output "$Image is not in the task folder"; exit 1 }

templates.name: Dell-ApplyUpdates
templates.description: Install Dell driver and BIOS updates with Dell Command | Update
templates.notes: Needs the Dell Command Update application pack in the same answer file; it installs first.
text: if not exist %DCU% (echo Dell Command Update is not installed & exit /b 1)
rem 0 = updated, 1 = restart needed, 500 = nothing to update

templates.name: Autopilot-HardwareHash
templates.description: Collect the Windows Autopilot hardware hash for Intune and save it to the share
templates.notes: Replace REPLACE_SHARE with a folder such as \\server\Deploy\Autopilot (Domain Computers need write access, as for Status); add -GroupTag Staff to tag the PCs. A copy always stays in C:\Windows\Temp. Merge the files with Merge-AutopilotCsv (src\Autopilot.psm1) and import the CSV in Intune > Devices > Windows enrollment > Devices.
text: # The same hash Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo reads: Windows 10 1703 or later, run as SYSTEM or an administrator.
if (-not $dev.DeviceHardwareData) { throw 'No hardware hash from WMI (MDM_DevDetail_Ext01).' }
$lines = @('Device Serial Number,Windows Product ID,Hardware Hash' + $(if ($GroupTag) { ',Group Tag' } else { '' }))
} else { Write-Output "Autopilot hash for $serial saved to $env:windir\Temp\$name" }
